one_month_reasoning: Nothing company-specific is scheduled before 2026-12-16. Q4 results come in late February 2027, and the dividend record date (2026-12-11, $0.42) is immaterial. The open items are an FTC settlement announcement, which could land at any time (the company says talks are ongoing and the outcome could exceed the $1B already booked), and Middle East and airfare news. The Q3 beat and soft Q4 guide are already priced: the stock was $155.67 on Nov 3 and $157.53 on Nov 16. So the ladder is centered on today's price, lognormal at the stock's monthly volatility (39%/3.5 = 11.1%), with no drift.

fair_value.method: P/E of 14.6x on my NTM EPS at the horizon (~$12.80, FY2028-weighted) less the FTC and tax adjustments (-$2.03/share) = $184.82. The 14.6x keeps 0.8 of BKNG's discount to the EXPE/ABNB median of 22.5x.

downside.story: 10th percentile: a 2027 travel slowdown (Middle East conflict and high airfares persist, European demand softens) plus AI-agent channels taking share: room nights 5% below base in every forecast quarter (FY2027 ~flat y/y), take rate 10 bp lower (flights mix, agent fees), marketing/GB +15 bp (paid AI referrals and Google/DMA costs), and the market keeps de-rating the name to ~11.6x NTM EPS (EXPE-like 15x less a disintermediation discount).

base.story: Median: travel normalizes in 2027 (room nights +5-7%), ADR +3%, take rate drifts down 10 bp on flights mix, marketing flat, and opex grows ~6.5% with transformation savings, so the EBIT margin holds at ~35%. Buybacks cut the share count 6.5% a year, NTM EPS is ~$12.80 at the horizon, and the P/E re-rates modestly from 13.1x to 14.6x.

upside.story: 90th percentile: travel recovers as the conflict fades, room nights 3% above base (FY2027 ~+8%), B2C marketing leverage 10 bp/GB as direct and app mix rise and LLM referrals prove incremental, and the AI-disruption discount narrows to ~17.6x NTM EPS (still below the 22.5x peer median).

reasoning: Primary-document build. The Q3 2026 10-Q, release and transcript give actuals (room nights 345M +7%, gross bookings $54.5B +10%, adjusted revenue $9.79B, take rate -15 bp) and the Q4 guide (room nights 1-3%, adjusted revenue 0-2%, EBITDA about flat). The $900M FTC revenue reduction plus a $100M accrual is booked as a one-off and an equity adjustment. The record: annual first revenue guides were beaten in FY2024 (+3.4% vs mid) and FY2025 (+8.0%), but FY2026's first guide (low double digits) is now a ~3% miss, so I give no beat premium. Drivers: room nights from global travel demand (UN Tourism 2026 cut to +1-2%) plus a share-gain spread narrowed from ~4.5 pts to ~2 for AI and competition; ADR +3% (CFO); take rate down 10 bp/yr on flights mix; marketing flat as a share of GB; non-marketing opex +6.6% net of the $650M transformation run-rate. FY2027 revenue is $31.4B (consensus $31.5B, StockAnalysis 2026-11-13) and EPS ~$11.7 (consensus adjusted $12.23, ~4% below). Buybacks of ~$9B/yr cut shares 6.5%/yr. Valuation: P/E on horizon NTM EPS, exit 14.6x from the k = 0.8 shrink of 13.1x toward the 22.5x two-peer median, giving a research target (12m) of $184.82 (+17%). The downside (P10, $123) and upside (P90, $243) move room nights, take rate and marketing and ±3 turns of multiple; the left tail is fatter, consistent with 39% realized volatility. The room-night spread is the biggest judgment call (±7-10%), flagged for Kilian. Research was limited: numeric Q2/Q3 2026 quarter guides and a 2027 UN Tourism forecast were not found, and the SEC refused direct curl (filings read via WebFetch and the cached companyfacts).

downside.story: 10th percentile: a 2027 travel slowdown (Middle East conflict and high airfares persist, European demand softens) plus AI-agent channels taking share: room nights 5% below base in every forecast quarter (FY2027 ~flat y/y), take rate 10 bp lower (flights mix, agent fees), marketing/GB +15 bp (paid AI referrals and Google/DMA costs), and the market keeps de-rating the name to ~11.6x NTM EPS (EXPE-like 15x less a disintermediation discount).

upside.story: 90th percentile: travel recovers as the conflict fades, room nights 3% above base (FY2027 ~+8%), B2C marketing leverage 10 bp/GB as direct and app mix rise and LLM referrals prove incremental, and the AI-disruption discount narrows to ~17.6x NTM EPS (still below the 22.5x peer median).

inputs_detail.derivation: Economic driver = global travel demand (UN Tourism international arrivals, src 10: 2025 +4% is not on that page; the page gives H1 2026 +0.4% and the full-year 2026 forecast cut to +1-2% from the January +3-4%) times BKNG's capture spread. BKNG room nights grew 6.0% YTD 2026 (1,008M vs 951M) against arrivals of ~+1-2%, a spread of ~4.5 pts, helped by domestic travel (CFO Steenbergen, src 3: domestic high single digits, international mid single digits). Q4 FY2026 +2.5% y/y (292.1M): October disruptions (Middle East, European unrest; CFO, src 3) and the toughest comp of the year; the company guide is 1-3% (src 2) and Q3 beat the top of its guide (CFO, src 3), so I sit just above the midpoint, not at the top. FY2027 +5% in Q1-Q3 (arrivals assumed +3%, the bottom of UN Tourism's January 2026 3-4% range as the conflict fades, plus a spread narrowed to ~2 pts for rising AI/meta-search and alternative-accommodation competition) and +7% in Q4 FY2027 against the depressed Q4 FY2026 base; FY2028 +5% (arrivals +3%, spread +2). Alternatives: (a) hold the YTD 2026 spread of 4.5 pts on +3% arrivals = +7.5%/yr (upside); (b) UN Tourism's 2026 forecast +1.5% plus spread 2 = +3.5%; (c) consensus revenue FY2027 $31.5B (src 9) implies ~+8% revenue, consistent with ~5% room nights. Variant: an AI-agent channel shift that cuts the spread to 0 gives ~+3%/yr and ~-6% value.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Holding the YTD 2026 spread (+4.5% level) = +9.8% value; UN Tourism 2026 pace (-3% level) = -6.6% (engine-sized).

model_inputs.structure_note: Quarterly driver-led set (16 quarters, 7 reported). Five drivers: room nights x gross bookings per room night = gross bookings; x take rate = revenue; less marketing (% of GB) and non-marketing opex ($M) = operating income on a GAAP basis (SBC expensed); one-off constants reproduce GAAP actuals (FTC, KAYAK impairment, restructuring). One leg carries the value: P/E on the build's own NTM EPS at the horizon (BKNG is Consumer Discretionary, so no FCF-yield leg), with three equity adjustments (FTC accrual, FTC above-accrual risk, unrecognized tax benefits). No SOTP: Booking.com is ~90% of the economics, and KAYAK/OpenTable are too small to value apart. No DCF (policy).
model_inputs.gap_note: For Kilian (judgment calls sized with the engine): (1) room-night path: holding the YTD 2026 share-gain spread (+4.5% level) moves the research target (12m) +9.8%; the UN Tourism 2026 pace (-3% level) moves it -6.6%. Both are over 5%, so they are cards. (2) ADR flat (-2% gbrn level): -4.4%. (3) Horizon P/E: EXPE alone 15.3x +4.8%; k = 1 (hold 13.1x) about -10%. That is a k choice over 5%, so it is a card. Take rate, marketing and opex alternatives each move it under 2%. Only 2 genuine listed peers (see comps_summary.peer_count_flag). fair_value.value equals the engine's base horizon value. Financing: none at >=20% probability; the $12.4B authorization is funded from cash flow.

comps_summary.peer_count_flag: 2 peers (EXPE, ABNB). Trip.com and MakeMyTrip are excluded for country distortion; UBER is mobility and delivery, and its GAAP EPS carries equity marks; Tripadvisor and Trivago are shrinking ad/meta-search businesses (TRIP 2026 EPS consensus -33%, stale page); eDreams has no consensus page on the same basis. Not padded.
